headlineRead: The regime remains stagflationary, but the freshest investable change is inside AI power infrastructure: Vertiv's agreement to buy UtilityInnovation Group adds microgrid controls, onsite-generation orchestration and behind-the-meter switchgear to its grid-to-chip stack. That directly validates time-to-power and microgrids as a monetising bottleneck. Refined-product scarcity also strengthened: European gasoline cracks neared records and diesel margins remained extreme, while EIA showed US crude and gasoline draws despite 98% refinery utilisation. Meanwhile ADP private payroll growth slowed to 38,000, sharpening the growth-versus-inflation squeeze.
whatsNewNow: VRT agreed to acquire UtilityInnovation Group for ~$1.45B cash plus up to $1.15B contingent consideration, adding microgrid controls, specialised switchgear and behind-the-meter power architecture. This materially strengthens the time-to-power thesis.
European gasoline margins surged above $62/bbl and diesel margins remained around the high-$70s over Brent, confirming that refined-product scarcity is broader than diesel alone.

EIA: US crude inventories fell 4.5M bbl to 424.5M, gasoline fell 1.2M bbl, refinery utilisation hit 98%, and East Coast distillates were at a record low; total product supplied nevertheless fell to 20.68 mbpd, a first demand-destruction warning.
ADP private payrolls rose only 38,000 in August, below expectations and July, while the 10Y still finished near 4.78% after touching ~4.81%. Growth is cooling before inflation pressure has cleared.
CF reached a record high as the Iran/LNG disruption tightened nitrogen supply economics. The thesis strengthened; the entry worsened.
Tesla's Sep 3 Cybercab event is now the most important holding-specific near-term catalyst; price recovered to ~$357 after trading below the old $353-355 support intraday.
whatMattersMostNow: Refined-product inflation and Hormuz physical disruption
Global long-end/real-yield stress despite weak hiring
AI time-to-power / microgrids and funded-load quality
Selective cyber/software pullbacks rather than blanket SaaS
